input.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
input.reasoning_summary:
The claim makes two assertions: (1) that overhead costs held steady as a share of sales in fiscal 2026, and (2) that workforce reductions were the main reason for this.

Regarding the first assertion (overhead costs as a share of sales held steady): The evidence does not provide specific data on overhead costs as a percentage of sales for fiscal 2026 overall. Evidence E4 mentions "SG&A as a percentage of net sales decreased due a decrease in overhead spending" for Q2 FY2026 (period ending 2025-12-31), but this refers to a decrease in SG&A percentage, not overhead costs holding steady. The fiscal 2026 10-K (E1) discusses drivers of SG&A changes generally but does not state that overhead costs as a share of sales held steady for the full year.

Regarding the second assertion (workforce reductions as the main reason): While the evidence mentions "workforce optimization" as part of cost improvement plans (E2, E3, E6) and discusses a restructuring program announced in June 2025 (E5), there is no passage that states workforce reductions were the main driver of overhead costs holding steady as a share of sales in fiscal 2026. The evidence discusses workforce optimization as one of several cost management strategies but does not attribute any specific outcome to it as the primary cause.

The claim is interpretive because it asserts a causal relationship (workforce reductions being the main reason). Without evidence explicitly stating this causation, the claim cannot be verified.
